brief.title: Business card: Crumb & Co. Bakery
brief.brief:
Design a two-sided US business card (3.5 x 2 in) for Crumb & Co. Bakery. It is open Tuesday to Sunday, 7am to 3pm, and takes preorders at crumbandco.example. Those are the only facts: do not add reviews, ratings, awards, a phone number, an address or anything else.

Deliver both sides as one self-contained HTML document (inline CSS and inline SVG only). On screen, show the front and the back as cards that scale fluidly to fit a phone and a desktop without sideways scrolling; you may add a short screen-only note beside the cards (not on them) stating the trim size and how to print. For print, add an @media print block with @page { size: 3.5in 2in; margin: 0 } so it prints as exactly two pages, page 1 the front and page 2 the back, each filling its page, with any screen-only notes hidden.

requirements.description: Shows the bakery name "Crumb & Co. Bakery" on the card.
States the hours: Tuesday to Sunday (Tue-Sun), 7am to 3pm.
Contains no invented reviews, ratings, awards or other facts beyond the brief, and presents a front and a back side.

artifacts.title: Crumb & Co. Bakery · Business Card (3.5 x 2 in)

render.note: KERNEL renders the watermarked preview (screen media only), exactly as for live entries.

judge.reason: The page meets all four requirements: the name, hours, preorder line and both sides are present, with no invented facts.

checks.reason: The back card shows "Crumb & Co. Bakery" as a header line, and the front headline reads "Crumb & Co. Bakery" split across two lines with the ampersand styled in the accent colour.
The back card shows the "Tue–Sun" label, "Tuesday to Sunday" in bold, and "7am to 3pm" in the accent colour.
The back card footer reads "Preorders at crumbandco.example" as a link. The front also says "Preorders open online at crumbandco.example".

The copy contains only the brief's facts plus the decorative word "Bakery" and the "Hours" tag. No reviews, ratings, awards, phone number or address appear, and both a front and a back section are present.

narrative.overall_verdict: A restrained, well-organised two-sided card that carries exactly the brief's facts. The front and back are clearly separated, and the back's hours block has a clear hierarchy.
strengths: Back side has a clear hierarchy: name, small Tue–Sun label, bold "Tuesday to Sunday", then the accent-coloured "7am to 3pm".
Warm paper palette with a brown accent suits a bakery and stays consistent across both sides.
Cards scale to the 390px phone width with no sideways overflow, per the browser measurement.
weaknesses: Front headline wraps onto two tight lines and the italic tagline sits almost directly under "Bakery", which looks cramped.
The front's small "BAKERY" eyebrow repeats the name, adding little information.
On a phone the italic tagline and small caps labels are quite small and light, so they will be hard to read.
narrative.best_for: best if you want a plain, typographic card that states only the hours and preorder details

artifacts.title: Crumb & Co. Bakery | Business Card (3.5 x 2 in)

render.note: KERNEL renders the watermarked preview (screen media only), exactly as for live entries.

judge.reason: The page meets all four requirements: it shows the name, hours, days, preorder line and a front and back with no invented facts, and it fits a 390px phone without sideways scroll.

checks.reason: The front card shows the name as an h1 split across lines: "Crumb & Co." then "Bakery", with the ampersand in the accent colour. The screenshots show the full name on both desktop and phone.
The back card shows "7am to 3pm" in large type under a "Hours" label, with "Tuesday to Sunday (Tue-Sun)" beneath it. Both appear in the desktop and phone screenshots.
The mint pill on the back reads "Preorders at crumbandco.example" and is visible in both screenshots.

The page contains only the brief's facts: name, hours, days, and preorder URL. There are no reviews, ratings, awards, phone number or address. It has a separate front and back, and the screen-only note is hidden when printing.

narrative.overall_verdict: A clean, friendly two-sided card that presents every fact the brief supplied on the correct side and invents nothing. The front is name-only, and the back carries the hours and preorder line in a clear hierarchy.
strengths: The back puts "7am to 3pm" in the largest type, so the hours are the first thing read.
The preorder URL sits in a mint pill, which sets it apart from the hours block.
Only the brief's facts appear, with no reviews, contact details or invented claims.
weaknesses: The front carries no information beyond the name, so a customer gets no reason to read the back.
The small "Tuesday to Sunday (Tue-Sun)" line is noticeably smaller than the hours and would be harder to read at print size.
The decorative wave borders and loaf icon take up space that could hold more legible text.
narrative.best_for: Best if you want a soft, illustrated card with the hours and preorder link as the clear focus.

render.note: KERNEL renders the watermarked preview (screen media only), exactly as for live entries.

judge.reason: The submission meets all four requirements: name, hours, preorders, and no invented facts, with a front and back side.

checks.reason: The front shows the h1 "Crumb & Co. Bakery" in large type, plus a kicker reading "Crumb & Co."; the full name appears in the desktop and phone screenshots.
The back reads "HOURS" then "TUESDAY TO SUNDAY (TUE-SUN)" and "7am to 3pm" in both the desktop and phone screenshots.
Both sides show "Preorders at crumbandco.example" in a dark bar on the front and an orange bar on the back.
The page contains only the brief's facts plus a screen-only note on trim size and printing; no reviews, ratings, awards, phone, or address appear, and front and back sections are both present.

narrative.overall_verdict: A clean, high-contrast two-sided card that uses only the brief's facts. The orange front and near-black back are easy to read, and the hours are set large on the back.
strengths: Front uses a bold orange field with the name set in heavy uppercase, giving strong brand presence.
Back sets the hours in large orange type, so the 7am to 3pm line is the clear focal point.
Phone layout fits the 390px screen with no sideways overflow, and the cards scale with the viewport.
weaknesses: The front repeats the name as a small kicker above the large heading, which adds clutter without new information.
The screen note sits above the cards and takes space on a phone before the card is visible.
The back's day line is set in white on near-black, but the hours block has little supporting detail, so it reads sparse.
narrative.best_for: Best if you want a bold, minimal card that puts the hours and preorder address up front.
